chunks: And from him, raising it, from Abū ʿAbdillāh (عليه السلام), who said:
Rasūl Allāh (صلى الله عليه وآله) said: “O ʿAlī, indeed Allah has made poverty a trust among His creatures.”

So whoever conceals it, Allah will give him the like of the reward of one who fasts and stands in worship; and whoever discloses it to one who is able to fulfill his need, but he does not do so, then he has killed him.
Indeed, he did not kill him with a sword or a spear, but rather he killed him by the hurt he inflicted upon his heart.”

key_terms.أَجْرِ الصَّائِمِ الْقَائِمِ: the reward of one who fasts and stands in worship
key_terms.أَمَانَةً: a trust placed in one's care, requiring protection and discretion
key_terms.الْفَقْرَ: poverty, understood here as a state of need and deprivation
key_terms.سَتَرَهُ: concealed it, meaning he did not expose his poverty to others
key_terms.قَتَلَهُ: killed him, meaning caused devastating moral and emotional harm
key_terms.قَلْبِهِ: his heart, the locus of inner pain and injury

ai.seo_question: What does this hadith teach about concealing poverty and the duty to help the needy?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches that poverty is a trust that should be concealed with dignity rather than exposed unnecessarily. It condemns the emotional and moral harm caused when a needy person reveals his need to someone capable of helping, yet is refused, describing that wound to the heart as a kind of killing. The narration emphasizes compassion, preserving dignity, and the grave responsibility of responding to need.
